about.title: Personal Injury Help in Whittier, California
about.longDescription: Whittier sits in the southeastern part of Los Angeles County, and its main streets carry a lot of daily traffic. Public records for 2025, the most recent complete year, show 443 injury collisions inside city limits, leaving 599 people hurt and 7 people dead. The largest share of those reports came from four corridors: Whittier Boulevard, Lambert Road, Beverly Boulevard and Painter Avenue. Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. account for the busiest stretch of the week. Behind every one of those numbers is someone dealing with an emergency room bill, a car that no longer runs, or a job they can't get back to yet. If that describes you, LawProactive can help you find your footing. We are a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Whittier and the rest of Los Angeles County. We are not a law firm, and we do not give legal advice. What we do is listen to what happened, then match you with a lawyer who can evaluate your claim. The attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means no fee unless there is a recovery. Under California law you generally have two years to file, and shorter deadlines apply when a city or county is involved, so starting early matters.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Whittier Claim

items.title: Two Years, Sometimes Much Less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a government entity such as the City of Whittier, Los Angeles County or a transit agency may be responsible, the window to file a claim can be as short as six months.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Close the Door
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible for a crash on Lambert Road, your recovery is reduced by your share of the blame, but you are not barred from recovering.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary personal injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages. Your losses beyond medical bills and missed paychecks, such as pain, sleeplessness or lost enjoyment of daily life, can be part of the claim.

items.title: Contingency Fees, Not Retainers
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Where do most injury crashes in Whittier happen?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the highest counts in Whittier are reported along Whittier Boulevard, Lambert Road, Beverly Boulevard and Painter Avenue. These are simply the streets with the largest number of reported incidents, which tends to track with how heavily they are traveled. Records also show reports peaking on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Whittier?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. When a public agency may share responsibility, for example a city vehicle or a poorly maintained public roadway, a claim often must be filed within six months. Because these deadlines vary, it helps to talk with an attorney early.

items.question: What if the insurance company says I was partly to blame?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so partial responsibility does not eliminate your claim. Your compensation is reduced in proportion to your share of fault, whatever that percentage turns out to be. An attorney can review the police report and evidence to challenge an insurer's version of who was at fault.
